QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_44

question.text: What is the purpose of an inter-bond spread in interest rate derivatives?

answer.text: To profit from the changing price relationship between different GOI bond futures contracts
To hedge currency exposure using bond futures
To speculate on a single bond's price direction
To eliminate all market risk through diversification

explanation.text: The Logic: An inter-bond spread is a long-short futures position on different underlying GOI bonds (typically same expiry). Traders use it to express views on yield curve steepening or flattening, profiting from changes in the relative price between the two bond futures. The Trap: This has nothing to do with currency. It's a relative value trade, not directional. Spreads still carry risk if the relationship doesn't move as expected. Note: Inter-bond spreads are also called yield curve trades — taking a view on relative movement between tenors rather than absolute rate direction.
